title: Conversation execution provenance: the original execution mode, route and executor artifact of a reply attempt, and the executor a runtime receipt claims
why: A reply attempt's create body is scrubbed at its end, and its grant, runtime unit and hello change; none of them can say afterwards whether it ran in-process as a no-home service call or as a native child. The server now keeps, per attempt and immutably, the {execution, routeId, executorArtifactDigest} it dispatched under (migration 0067), and projects it to the runtime (FND-B2, V's provenance disposition).
A service attempt's create payload carries that tuple (payload.conversation.execution), so the executor compares it with its own installed, pinned service-only closure before anything runs.
The recovery binding of a service attempt carries the same tuple (provenance), so a fresh process can tell its own attempt from a native or unknown one; absent means native or unknown, never service.

A runtime receipt may state the executor that sends it (executor). It is a claim, checked by the server against its own stored provenance, never a source of it: a service attempt's checked retire requires the exact service tuple; a native or unknown attempt refuses a service claim. Native receipts without the field are unchanged.

value.description: A service attempt's original execution tuple, from the server's provenance (0067). Absent for a native attempt.
A service attempt's original execution tuple, as the server kept it at dispatch. Absent: native or unknown.
The executor sending this receipt, as it claims to be; the server checks it against its stored provenance for a conversation attempt. Absent: as before this amendment.
